logline: Eldest daughter Hannah Defoe defects from the family divorce firm to a rival practice, then finds her own marriage unravelling under the same forensic pressure she applies to her clients' crumbling unions.

renewal.note: Three main series concluded in May 2022, followed by a two-part special in December 2024. A spin-off, The Split Up, is in development.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 earned 74% on Rotten Tomatoes and a 72 Metacritic score - critics found the Defoe family sibling dynamic genuinely compelling and Nicola Walker's Hannah a finely calibrated lead, with reservations about the show's occasionally over-polished surface.

pull_quotes.text: This is where The Split really shines - the Defoe women face real decisions and consequences.
The trio's sibling dynamic is a delight, realistically but warmly observed.

seasons.review_body: Series 1 premiered on BBC One in April 2018, written by Abi Morgan, and earned 74% on Rotten Tomatoes with a 72 Metacritic score. Critics found the show's central conceit - a family of divorce lawyers whose own family is fracturing - dramatically rich if occasionally too neatly assembled. Paste Magazine praised the show when it allowed the Defoe women to 'face real decisions and consequences'. The Independent called the sibling dynamic 'a delight, realistically but warmly observed'. Nicola Walker's Hannah established immediately as a performance of controlled emotional precision, and her chemistry with Stephen Mangan as husband Nathan anchored a marriage the show would spend three series slowly and deliberately dismantling. The Times noted the show was 'often too polished for its own good' while acknowledging its pleasures.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 improved to 78% on Rotten Tomatoes as the Hannah-Nathan marriage tension deepened and the show's family firm dynamics grew more entangled and dramatically productive.

pull_quotes.text: Walker and Mangan are still great at understated comedy and digging out emotional truths.

seasons.review_body: Series 2 aired in February-March 2020 and earned 78% on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics noted an improvement in the show's confidence - the Walker-Mangan central dynamic had deepened into something more complex and less polished than the debut season's surface-sheen. The Telegraph praised both leads for their 'understated comedy and emotional truth'. The Wall Street Journal, after initial reservations, noted the show found 'its footing as powerful drama' once its wandering subplots resolved. The family firm subplot - with Fiona Button and Annabel Scholey as Hannah's sisters - generated the most praised ensemble scenes of the series, and Deborah Findlay as matriarch Ruth provided the emotional backbone that held the family dynamics together.
seasons.season_over_season: A step up from Season 1 - the Hannah-Nathan marriage unravels with more complexity and less polish than the debut.

bollymeter.basis: The concluding series resolved Hannah and Nathan's arc to broadly positive critical reception - audiences who had invested three seasons found the emotional payoff handled with the quiet intelligence the series had developed.

seasons.review_body: Series 3 aired April-May 2022 as the main narrative conclusion of The Split, bringing Hannah and Nathan's long-running marital dissolution to a resolution the show had earned through three seasons of patient character work. Abi Morgan's writing had by Series 3 moved past the show's early reputation as glossy BBC drama - the audience consensus of 91% on Rotten Tomatoes overall reflected an investment that deepened with each series. The three-season arc demonstrated something rare: a drama whose understanding of its characters genuinely sharpened over time, allowing Nicola Walker and Stephen Mangan to deliver performances of increasing subtlety. The December 2024 two-part special provided a coda for those who wanted further resolution.
seasons.season_over_season: The strongest entry in dramatic terms - three seasons of careful character investment pay off in the concluding episodes.
